doc.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
doc.interviewee: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum

title: Band rehearsals at home and George's music
summary: Charlotte recalls bands passing the house on wagons and rehearsals in the house; Mrs. McCullum says he composed nothing she knew of but left a box of music.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: It was, well, everything was fine then because whenever they would, you know, play jobs and whatnot, they'd always stop in front of the house, you know. I can remember thinking we'd all run out as children, you know. And they'd have this, they would play in wagons and trucks and things and whatnot, you know. Old furniture wagons. Old furniture wagons and whatnot, you know. And then they would have them pass our house. And frankly, between Louise and Eve and Darrell Shays, and they'd stop and play us a number, you know. I've heard how they advertise. It's real fun. Yeah. If it's real fun.
Just for your... And all that rehearsal in my house, which every fall, I'd give you...
That's all we can remember. One room that rehearsed. All we can remember from Papa's to Little George, you know. You did us. Having a band in the house playing. And we could sleep through all that.
Sleep through all. Did he ever compose any numbers of his own?

Who, my husband? Yeah. No. Not that I know of him. If he did, I don't remember. But, Lord, he had all kinds of music. After he died, I had a big box of music. I told him, Mama, that would have been so useful now. Oh, I know. The Lord, the Reigners. Now you don't know it. Money. My son had some of the music. Some of the copies before he died. And he used to say to me, he made me start all of his music out. And he said, put out the valuable music. He says, now, don't you let nobody take this. Someday you might need a piece of bread. Tell me. You might need a piece of bread and you can sell that. Yeah. But I turned all that over to George, my son. Don't know what that's.
Well, maybe somebody got some good out of it, I hope.
I hope because I hope he got too good of it.
